# City- and Season-Aware Multi-Pollutant Air Quality Assessment and Forecasting Framework for Indian Cities Using Deep Learning

*Final report (auto-generated by Part 7, run 20261103_190852). Six-pollutant estimated AQI using CPCB sub-index methodology.*

> **Scope note.** NH3 and Pb are unavailable, so this is not the official CPCB AQI. O3/CO values are Open-Meteo/CAMS-based estimates, not direct CPCB ground-station observations. The framework provides decision support, not definitive source attribution or regulatory enforcement.

## 1. Abstract

This study builds a city- and season-aware framework for estimating and forecasting air quality across 101 Indian cities (2022-08-04 to 2026-07-20; 146,147 city-days) using Open-Meteo/CAMS-based pollutant and weather estimates. A six-pollutant estimated AQI (CPCB sub-index methodology; NH3 and Pb unavailable) is computed from daily means and 8-hour maxima, and the dominant pollutant is summarised for every city and season (404 city-season cells) with rule-based, suggestive weather explanations. Persistence, classical machine-learning and deep-learning models (LSTM, GRU, 1D-CNN, CNN-LSTM, Bi-LSTM with attention) were compared on one chronological train/validation/test split. For next-day AQI regression the model selected on validation was GRU (Deep learning; test RMSE 43.81 vs 48.70 for persistence). For category classification the selected model was XGBoost (test macro-F1 0.625 vs 0.652 for persistence). For the 3-day high-risk warning (AQI > 200) the selected model was GRU (test PR-AUC 0.915). Results are reported with uncertainty intervals and should be read as predictive performance on this dataset, not as causal evidence.

## 2. Introduction

Air-quality management benefits from short-term forecasts that also say *which pollutant* is likely to drive a poor-air day and *why that may be so*. This project combines (i) an estimated multi-pollutant AQI, (ii) a city x season description of dominant pollutants with weather-based, suggestive explanations, and (iii) forecasting models for next-day AQI, next-day category and a 3-day high-risk warning. All statements about causes are interpretations of associations and are phrased accordingly.

## 3. Dataset and source limitations

The daily dataset covers 101 cities from 2022-08-04 to 2026-07-20 (146,147 city-days) with PM2.5, PM10, CO, NO2, SO2, O3 (daily means, ug/m3), temperature, humidity, wind speed and rainfall. **The values are Open-Meteo/CAMS-based estimates, not direct CPCB ground-station observations.** Original files were never modified; every processed output is versioned.

- Part 1 validation found 0 rows with PM2.5 > PM10, which indicates estimation inconsistency; they were flagged, not deleted.
- 1 city pairs have identical series across all pollutants and 7 pairs for PM2.5 alone; this is consistent with a coarse spatial grid assigning the same cell to nearby cities (not a definitive explanation).
- Extreme observations were flagged and retained; 2040 PM10 city-days exceed the per-city Q3 + 3 x IQR fence.

## 4. Methodology

The framework is a seven-part pipeline: (1) loading, validation and hourly O3/CO retrieval; (2) estimated AQI and EDA; (3) weather-based explanations and policy rules; (4) leakage-safe features, chronological split and train-only scaling; (5) classical ML; (6) 30-day sequence deep learning; (7) synthesis, ablation, explainability and reporting.

## 5. Hourly O3/CO retrieval and 8-hour maximum calculation

Hourly ozone and carbon monoxide were requested from the Open-Meteo Air Quality API for each unique city coordinate (local time, Asia/Kolkata). A trailing 8-hour mean (at least 6 valid hours) is computed per city; the daily maximum of these means (at least 18 valid windows per day) gives O3_8hr_max (ug/m3) and CO_8hr_max, converted to mg/m3 for the CO sub-index. Original daily means are left unchanged.
**Coverage note:** 101 of 146,147 city-days (0.1%) still use the provisional daily-mean fallback for O3 and/or CO (hourly data could not be retrieved for those days). Their O3/CO sub-indices are therefore provisional and likely understate 8-hour peaks.

## 6. AQI estimation

**Six-pollutant estimated AQI using CPCB sub-index methodology.** Sub-indices for PM2.5, PM10, NO2 and SO2 use 24-hour (daily) means; O3 uses the 8-hour maximum (ug/m3) and CO the 8-hour maximum (mg/m3). Estimated AQI is the maximum sub-index and the dominant pollutant is the pollutant attaining it (ties go to PM2.5, PM10, NO2, SO2, O3, CO in that order). Categories: Good 0-50, Satisfactory 51-100, Moderate 101-200, Poor 201-300, Very Poor 301-400, Severe 401-500. NH3 and Pb are unavailable, so this is not the official CPCB AQI.
The CPCB tables are open-ended in the Severe band; the upper ends used for interpolation and the 500 cap are an assumption of this framework: {'PM2_5': 380, 'PM10': 510, 'NO2': 520, 'SO2': 2400, 'O3': 1288, 'CO': 51} (2,385 city-days reached the cap).

## 7. Feature engineering

Past-only features per city (172 features): current-day values, lags (1, 2, 3, 7 days), rolling means (3, 7, 14, 30 days) and standard deviations (7, 30 days) computed after a one-day shift, calendar and cyclic terms, season indicators, interaction terms (PM2.5/PM10, NO2+CO, SO2/PM2.5, temperature x O3, wind x PM2.5, rainfall x PM10, humidity x PM2.5), and city/region context. Targets are the AQI and category at t+1 and a binary indicator of AQI > 200 within the next three days. Perturbation tests confirmed that scrambling future observations leaves earlier features unchanged.

## 8. City and season awareness

City awareness enters through a city identifier (embedding for deep models), region, latitude and longitude; season awareness through season indicators and cyclic calendar terms. Regime awareness uses K-Means pollution-weather regimes fitted on the training split only (k = 3). The primary descriptive product is the 101 x 4 city-season table (observed dominant pollutant, mean and median concentrations, mean AQI, share of days with AQI > 200, likely cause).

## 9. Weather-based dominant-pollutant explanation

Rule-based statements link simultaneous weather and concentration patterns (e.g., low wind and little rain with elevated particulates) to possible contributors. They **suggest** plausible influences and are **consistent with** known meteorology; they do not attribute emissions to sources. Counts of cities by observed most-frequent dominant pollutant:

| Season | O3 | PM10 | PM2_5 | SO2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Winter | 72 | 0 | 29 | 0 |
| Summer | 91 | 10 | 0 | 0 |
| Monsoon | 99 | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| Post-monsoon | 96 | 0 | 5 | 0 |

## 10. Models

Baselines: persistence (tomorrow equals today). Classical ML: Ridge / Logistic regression, Random Forest, XGBoost. Deep learning on 30-day sequences with city and region embeddings: LSTM, GRU, 1D-CNN, CNN-LSTM and Bi-LSTM with attention (regression, category classification; LSTM, GRU and Bi-LSTM-attention for the high-risk task). Deep-learning regression outputs are converted to AQI units with the saved RobustScaler.

## 11. Experimental setup

One global chronological split (all cities together): train 2022-09-03 to 2025-05-20, validation 2025-05-21 to 2025-12-19, test 2025-12-20 to 2026-07-19; the last 7 dates of train and validation were purged so that multi-day labels cannot overlap the next split. 
Scaling used a RobustScaler fitted on training data only. Models were fitted on train, tuned or early-stopped on validation, and scored once on test. All models were compared on identical test rows. Uncertainty is shown with a moving-block bootstrap over test dates (500 draws, 7-day blocks). Seed 42.
The test period contains the seasons: Winter, Summer, Monsoon; seasonal conclusions are limited to these.

A one-day-ahead AQI series is strongly autocorrelated, so persistence is a demanding baseline; gains over it should be judged against the intervals above. For the high-risk warning (GRU, threshold 0.49 chosen on validation), the test period contains 8,683 high-risk city-days out of 21,210; the model issued 9,206 alerts (7,399 true, 1,807 false) and missed 1,284 events.

## 14. Explainability

Grouped permutation importance on held-out (validation and test) rows for the full-feature explainer model ranks: Estimated_AQI (current+lags+rolling) (58.82), PM10 (current+lags+rolling) (4.24), Regime (K-Means) (1.40), City identity (ID/region/lat/lon) (1.04), Calendar & season (0.31), Weather x pollutant interactions (0.30). City-wise and season-wise importance tables (final_feature_importance.csv) show how the leading groups shift across cities and seasons; shifts are consistent with different drivers, but they remain model associations.
Part 5 SHAP (validation sample) highlights: Estimated_AQI, Estimated_AQI, O3_8hr_max, O3_8hr_max, Estimated_AQI_roll30_mean.
Bi-LSTM attention is concentrated on the most recent days (highest weights at lags 0, 1, 2 days before the origin date), indicating the model relies mostly on recent history.

Case studies of major episodes (held-out period):

- **Panipat (Winter, peak 2026-03-01)**: observed AQI 500 (Severe); one-day-ahead prediction 258; dominant pollutant on the origin day PM10. Rule-based note (suggestive): Winter conditions may worsen particulate accumulation due to reduced atmospheric ventilation. The pattern suggests a dust-dominated contribution. Elevated NO2 and CO patterns are commonly associated with traffic and combustion-related emissions.
- **Alwar (Summer, peak 2025-05-22)**: observed AQI 500 (Severe); one-day-ahead prediction 298; dominant pollutant on the origin day PM10. Rule-based note (suggestive): Dry conditions and dust resuspension may contribute to elevated PM10. The pattern suggests a dust-dominated contribution.
- **Bilaspur (Monsoon, peak 2025-06-10)**: observed AQI 310 (Very Poor); one-day-ahead prediction 215; dominant pollutant on the origin day O3. Rule-based note (suggestive): Warm and sunny conditions favour photochemical ozone formation. Low wind speed and low rainfall favour accumulation of particulate pollution.
- **Mumbai (Post-monsoon, peak 2025-10-18)**: observed AQI 335 (Very Poor); one-day-ahead prediction 276; dominant pollutant on the origin day O3. Rule-based note (suggestive): Warm and sunny conditions favour photochemical ozone formation. Elevated NO2 and CO patterns are commonly associated with traffic and combustion-related emissions. Elevated SO2 may indicate industrial or fossil-fuel combustion influence.
- **Kashipur (Winter, peak 2025-12-28)**: observed AQI 347 (Very Poor); one-day-ahead prediction 293; dominant pollutant on the origin day PM2_5. Rule-based note (suggestive): Low wind speed and low rainfall favour accumulation of particulate pollution. Winter conditions may worsen particulate accumulation due to reduced atmospheric ventilation. High humidity may support secondary particle formation and pollutant retention. Elevated NO2 and CO patterns are commonly associated with traffic and combustion-related emissions. Elevated SO2 may indicate industrial or fossil-fuel combustion influence.

## 15. Limitations

- Data are Open-Meteo/CAMS-based estimates, not direct CPCB ground-station observations.
- AQI is a six-pollutant estimated AQI, not the official CPCB AQI.
- NH3 and Pb are unavailable.
- O3 and CO AQI sub-indices use 8-hour rolling maxima from re-fetched hourly Open-Meteo data (with 101 city-days, 0.1%, on a provisional daily-mean fallback).
- Identical city-series pairs may occur due to coarse spatial grid resolution.
- Extreme PM10 values were retained (flagged, not removed), so error metrics are influenced by them.
- The framework provides decision support, not definitive source attribution or regulatory enforcement.
- The test period spans 3 season(s) (Winter, Summer, Monsoon) of a roughly four-year record; seasonal generalisation is limited.
- Cause and policy statements are rule-based and threshold-dependent (thresholds are dataset-relative); they were not validated against emission inventories.
- Deep-learning results come from a single seed; GPU non-determinism and tuning limited to early stopping mean small differences between models should not be over-interpreted.

## 16. Future work

Use verified CPCB station data for calibration and validation; add NH3 and Pb when available; use finer spatial reanalysis to avoid duplicated city series; extend the record so every season appears in each split (or use rolling-origin evaluation); test multi-seed and probabilistic forecasts; add uncertainty-aware alerts and evaluate policy rules with local authorities; include emission-inventory and fire-count data for better-grounded attribution studies.

## 17. Conclusion

Within the limits of Open-Meteo/CAMS-based estimates and a six-pollutant estimated AQI, the framework describes dominant pollutants by city and season, forecasts next-day AQI and category, and issues a 3-day high-risk warning. For next-day AQI the selected model is clearly better than persistence on the test dates.  The weather- and city-aware components are reported with ablation evidence and uncertainty intervals so that readers can judge how much each contributes. The outputs support decision-making and do not replace regulatory monitoring.
